record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: When constructing an interaction network from time-stamped observations of a social organization using a sliding aggregation window or a time threshold Delta t, how should the window size or threshold be chosen so that network density, topological analyses, and reconstructed temporal paths for possible influence are reliable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{E} = \{(u_i, v_i, t_i)\}_{i=1}^N$ be a finite set of time-stamped pairwise interaction records among a population $V$ of agents of a social organization, where each $(u_i, v_i, t_i)$ records an observed interaction between agents $u_i, v_i \in V$ at time $t_i \in [T_{\min}, T_{\max}]$. For a window length $\Delta t > 0$ and a placement parameter $s \in \mathbb{R}$, define the aggregated (static) interaction graph $G_{s,\Delta t} = (V, E_{s,\Delta t})$ by
\[ E_{s,\Delta t} = \{\{u,v\} : \exists\, i \text{ with } \{u_i,v_i\}=\{u,v\} \text{ and } t_i \in [s, s+\Delta t)\}, \]
and the sequence of sliding-window graphs $\{G_{k\Delta t, \Delta t}\}_{k}$ covering $[T_{\min},T_{\max}]$. From these graphs one computes:
(i) the network density $\rho(\Delta t) = |E|/\binom{|V|}{2}$;
(ii) topological summary statistics such as clustering coefficient, degree distribution, and community structure;
(iii) the temporal (time-respecting) reachability graph $R(\Delta t)$ in which a directed edge $u \to v$ is present if there exists a sequence $(u=w_0, w_1, \dots, w_m=v)$ and times $\tau_1 \le \tau_2 \le \cdots \le \tau_m$ with each $\{w_{j-1}, w_j\}$ active in a window containing $\tau_j$, thereby reconstructing possible paths of influence.

Problem. Provide a principled, data-driven prescription for selecting the window/threshold parameter $\Delta t$ (and, if relevant, its placement $s$) such that the resulting quantities $\rho(\Delta t)$, the topological summaries of $\{G_{k\Delta t,\Delta t}\}$, and the temporal reachability $R(\Delta t)$ are reliable in the sense that they (a) are stable under small perturbations of $\Delta t$, (b) avoid the over-sparsification regime where most windows are nearly empty, (c) avoid the over-aggregation regime where genuine temporal ordering and dynamics are washed out, and (d) faithfully reflect the underlying causal/influence structure of the interactions. Specifically, derive conditions on $\Delta t$ — expressed in terms of statistics of the interaction time series (e.g., inter-event time distribution, burstiness, characteristic mixing or correlation time) — that simultaneously satisfy criteria (a)–(d), and prove the validity of any such criterion.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of principled selection of the aggregation window for temporal networks remains open in general. Existing literature (Krings et al., EPJ Data Science; Caceres & Berger-Wolf; Sulo et al.; and more recent adaptive data-driven methods, 2024) provides partial frameworks—balancing noise reduction against information loss, or identifying "meaningful" resolutions via structural change detection—but no universally accepted criterion exists that simultaneously guarantees reliability of density, topological analyses, and temporal-path reconstruction.

status_evidence.title: Effects of time window size and placement on the structure of an aggregated communication network
status_evidence.snippet: The aggregation time window is often dictated by the availability of data, and the effects of its length on the resulting networks are rarely considered.
status_evidence.claim: There is no established framework; window choice is typically ad hoc.

status_evidence.title: Meaningful selection of temporal resolution for dynamic networks
status_evidence.snippet: A framework for identifying meaningful resolution levels that best reveal critical changes in the network structure, by balancing the reduction of noise with the loss of information.
status_evidence.claim: Partial frameworks exist that balance noise vs information loss.

status_evidence.title: A time scale measurement method for dynamic temporal networks
status_evidence.snippet: An adaptive, data-driven method for selecting time scales to enhance the accuracy and reliability of dynamic temporal network analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) work proposes adaptive data-driven approaches, indicating the problem is still actively investigated.
